items.headline: BIO unveils plan for US to remain biotech’s ‘global leader’
items.preview: The Biotechnology Innovation Organization has proposed a plan to maintain U.S. leadership in biotech.
items.article:
Two months after China unveiled a five-year plan to accelerate its biotechnology sector, the Biotechnology Innovation Organization (BIO) has pitched a policy proposal to help the U.S. maintain its edge. The 'BioAdvance' plan outlines seven priorities for Congress and the administration to ensure the U.S. remains the global leader in biotech.

Why this matters: The U.S. has historically been a leader in drug development, but China's rapid advancements pose a significant challenge. BIO's proposal aims to enhance drug development efficiency, improve clinical trial infrastructure, and attract investment, while also calling for the establishment of a White House Office of Biotechnology to coordinate these efforts.

items.headline: Beam’s base editing therapy for sickle cell hits goal in pivotal trial
items.preview: Beam Therapeutics reports success in a pivotal trial for its gene editing treatment for sickle cell disease.
items.article:
Beam Therapeutics announced that its precision gene editing treatment, ristoglogene autogetemcel (risto-cel), has succeeded in a pivotal trial, helping patients with sickle cell disease avoid severe pain crises. This marks the first positive late-stage results for a base editing approach, with plans to submit an FDA approval application by year-end.

Why this matters: Risto-cel represents a new treatment option in a competitive landscape that includes existing therapies. Its success could pave the way for broader acceptance of base editing technologies in treating genetic disorders.

items.headline: SRTD raises €31.5M seed round to develop cell-selective RNA therapies
items.preview: SRTD Biotech secures €31.5 million to advance its RNA technology targeting specific cells.
items.article:
SRTD Biotech has successfully closed a €31.5 million seed funding round aimed at developing its selectively expressed RNA (seRNA) technology. This innovative approach seeks to activate therapeutic RNA only in target cells, minimizing harm to healthy tissues. The funding will support preclinical development in cancer, autoimmune diseases, and fibrosis.

Why this matters: The ability to selectively activate RNA therapies could revolutionize treatment options, particularly in oncology, by reducing side effects and improving efficacy.

items.headline: Dual-Energy CT Visualizes High-Grade Glioma Without Contrast
items.preview: A study shows dual-energy CT can visualize high-grade gliomas without contrast agents.
items.article:
Researchers at the University of Fukui have demonstrated that dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) can visualize high-grade gliomas similarly to gadolinium-enhanced MRI, without the need for contrast media. This method could benefit patients unable to undergo MRI due to various contraindications.

Why this matters: The ability to visualize tumors without contrast could expand diagnostic options for patients and enhance preoperative planning, particularly for those with conditions that limit MRI accessibility.

items.headline: PhagoCyt enables isolation of Salmonella-containing phagosomes
items.preview: A new method allows for the isolation of Salmonella-containing phagosomes for proteomic analysis.
items.article:
Researchers have developed a flow cytometry-based method called PhagoCyt to isolate Salmonella-containing phagosomes from macrophages. This technique enhances the analysis of host-pathogen interactions and provides insights into how Salmonella manipulates phagosome maturation.

Why this matters: The ability to isolate and analyze pathogen-containing phagosomes can significantly advance our understanding of bacterial survival strategies within host cells, potentially leading to new therapeutic approaches.
